newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sakura says former official held in fraud case.
newsitem.headline: Sakura says former official held in fraud case.

text.p: Sakura Bank Ltd said on Monday that police had arrested a former employee, who used to be deputy manager of one of the bank's branches, for alleged fraud.
A Sakura official told a news conference that the bank had already fired the official, who had been deputy manager of one of its branches in the Shibuya district of central Tokyo.

Police officials said the former Sakura official Takashi Okuyama and Makoto Yoshii, an executive of another company, allegedly told an official at one of Sakura's client companies earlier this year that they would manage funds for him.

The company official then entrusted 200 million yen to Okuyama and Yoshii for this purpose, the police officials said. It was not immediately clear whether the money came from the official's personal bank account or that of his company.
Police said they had also arrested Yoshii, but declined to disclose the name of Yoshii's company or that of the corporate client.
Police said the two men were likely to have been involved in other similar cases and that they were continuing investigations.
